cells.tense: You are here with the pen now, and the account is being kept cleanly.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take something that ended in the past year and, over a few lines in your own hand, set out what it left you. Note whether it changes what you do next — or that it doesn't.
cells.core: When the whole pattern is visible at once, you can still feel what is owed. A thing ends, and you can look at what it left behind and count it plainly, without making more or less of it. The count holds because you saw the ending through instead of outrunning it, and what came of it is sitting there to be taken in. Others look at the same field and go cold or go soft. You look, and the fairness survives the view. That is the ground under you right now, and it is being used rather than guarded. The waiting produced something you can name, and naming it is the whole of the next step.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole field, and the account comes out fair.
cells.verb: keeping the private account of what is fair
cells.place: the wide view where the whole pattern shows at once

cells.tense: You are bracing at a future that cannot be written in, and the account is running ahead of what has happened.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: Hand one person a real piece of help they are short on — something you have plenty of — and finish it before the week ends. Then stop; no follow-up.
cells.core: When the whole pattern is visible, every uneven edge of it shows at once, and you are settling all of them before they arrive. What should be a clear knowing of what is fair has become a running total of what will be owed, and the total keeps you up above the room. People can feel that you have already decided how it comes out, and they stop bringing you their half of it. Fairness moves through a room without you doing the sums when the thing is working. Aim your strength at one real shortage, finish it, and stop before the tally starts. The help need not be small to be finished in a week, only finished.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you, and the wide view is not being used.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Next time someone near you is stuck on a decision, describe the route you can see from where you sit, out loud, before you talk yourself out of it.
cells.core: You can see the whole pattern and you are not saying what you see. What you read stays private and unwritten, and from outside it looks like nothing is being weighed. The passage you can see is not being named, and others walk past it. Sight, not feeling, is what is missing here. A clear read of a situation offered plainly is not judgement — it is just the view from where you stand, and it takes nothing away from the person who needs it. The read has not left you; it has stopped coming out. Saying the route aloud is the smallest thing this does when it is working.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in, and the account is being kept without your name.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Take a sheet of paper and set out everything pulling at you right now — then mark beside each one whether it is yours or something you picked up from someone. Keep the sheet.
cells.core: You have been reading the whole pattern for a while and calling it what is obviously true. When something is off, you state it as though anyone would see the same thing, and it usually turns out you are right. Direct knowing lands without argument when the thing is working, and being comfortable not knowing is part of it. Right now what you see is steering things and being filed as plain fact, so nobody, including you, thinks to put your name on it. A borrowed pull and a real one look identical from the wide view. Marking which is which takes a page and a few minutes.
